findings.title: Reverse proxy headers are not trusted
findings.detail: gateway.bind is loopback and gateway.trustedProxies is empty. If you expose the Control UI through a reverse proxy, configure trusted proxies so local-client checks cannot be spoofed.
findings.remediation: Set gateway.trustedProxies to your proxy IPs or keep the Control UI local-only.

findings.title: Gateway auth missing on loopback
findings.detail: gateway.bind is loopback but no gateway auth secret is configured. If the Control UI is exposed through a reverse proxy, unauthenticated access is possible.
findings.remediation: Set gateway.auth (token recommended) or keep the Control UI local-only.

findings.title: Browser control has no auth
findings.detail: Browser control HTTP routes are enabled but no gateway.auth token/password is configured. Any local process (or SSRF to loopback) can call browser control endpoints.
findings.remediation: Set gateway.auth.token (recommended) or gateway.auth.password so browser control HTTP routes require authentication. Restarting the gateway will auto-generate gateway.auth.token when browser control is enabled.

findings.title: Small models require sandboxing and web tools disabled
findings.detail:
Small models (<=300B params) detected:
- ollama/qwen2.5:7b-instruct (7B) @ agents.defaults.model.primary (unsafe; sandbox=off; web=[web_search, web_fetch, browser])
Uncontrolled input tools allowed: web_search, web_fetch, browser.
Small models are not recommended for untrusted inputs.
findings.remediation: If you must use small models, enable sandboxing for all sessions (agents.defaults.sandbox.mode="all") and disable web_search/web_fetch/browser (tools.deny=["group:web","browser"]).

To open a pull request (PR) again, follow these steps:

1. **Ensure Your Branch Is Up-to-Date:**
   ```sh
   git pull origin main
   ```

2. **Make Your Changes:**
   - Add your code or make your changes.

3. **Commit Your Changes:**
   ```sh
   git add .
   git commit -m "Your descriptive commit message"
   ```

4. **Push Your Changes to the Remote Repository:**
   ```sh
   git push origin <your-branch>
   ```

5. **Create the Pull Request:**
   - Go to your repository on GitHub.
   - Click on the "Pull Requests" tab.
   - Click on the "New Pull Request" button.
   - Select the base repository and branch (usually `main` or `master`), and the source branch (your branch).
   - Add a title and description for the PR.
   - Click on "Create Pull Request."

Alternatively, you can use the `gh` CLI tool to create the pull request directly from the terminal:

```sh
gh pr create --title "Your PR title" --body "Your PR description" --base main --head <your-branch>
```
